correctness.rationale: All three letters occur by σ²(0). Substituting gives aa and a(a+1) for each a, and the junction in σ(aa) gives (a+1)a. These are all nine ordered pairs, with addition modulo 3. At rank m the fixed point is tiled by the images of its letters, each of length L=3^m, so every length-L factor lies in an occurring pair of consecutive blocks and all enumerated pair windows occur. Projection to (x₀,x₁) preserves the integer lattice in the affine plane, since x₂=L−x₀−x₁. Independent exact window counts and integer hull tests give the pairs (3,3), (10,10), (37,37), (115,136). The rank-three nine-vertex hull has twice area 237 and boundary lattice count 33, giving 136 by Pick's formula. Exact set subtraction gives exactly the cyclic rotations of (3,13,11), (3,15,9), (4,15,8), (5,7,15), (5,10,12), (6,6,15), (6,10,11), with seven disjoint size-three orbits. Thus rank three is the first nonsaturated power rank; no minimality over arbitrary lengths or higher-rank formula is asserted.

value.rationale: The natural next invariant after extremal counts and binary projections is the simultaneous attainable triple. The first gap between convex predictions and actual ternary factors shows exactly where those predictions cease to be complete at substitution scales, and the orbit list provides a reproducible benchmark for methods seeking full Parikh images. The power scales come from the intrinsic block structure, not an arbitrarily selected cutoff.
